_comment: Which cases of the shared Lua contracts moved into JSON vector corpora (PAR-58). Each moved entry names the removed case (an it title, or a loop's title prefix) and the vector ids that now hold it. tools/test/test-contract-vector-ledger.cjs fails when a vector is not listed here, when a listed vector is missing, when a removed case title is still registered in its contract, or when a vector breaks the schema.

families.entry_point: batch writer prepare step (source bytes + rows -> accepted, detail, candidate bytes)
families.windows_consumer: One AHK consumer calls the Windows TOML batch writer's prepare step for each vector and compares accepted, detail and candidate bytes; decoded checks use the Windows TOML codec.

moved.case: deletes a table declared by an empty header and keeps every comment
replaces a header table, its descendants and interleaved blocks by one scalar
removes a header table whose parent has no header of its own
leaves a value another spelling already holds byte-for-byte
rewrites a changed array of tables as one inline list and keeps its comments
updates and deletes a quoted bare-compatible key in place
names the key an inline table holds when its value changes
updates the existing section-inline string without owning its parent
refuses a batch that replaces a header table and writes inside it
publishes complete inline source:
retains exact nested dotted and quoted member fragments under a quoted header
preserves the explicit empty inline parent after its last scalar deletion
deletes an owned extension leaf while preserving all neighboring bytes
inserts and updates through equivalent literal and escaped section spellings
renders canonical colon segments as valid quoted TOML on first insertion
rejects equivalent batch rows before reading and preserves unrelated case variants
keeps quoted dots and bracket characters distinct from nested sections
rejects malformed table paths before acquiring a snapshot
refuses malformed source headers and equivalent duplicate tables
refuses ambiguous case-folded targets and array-of-table targets
